title: readParallelUnstructuredGrid
body:
## readParallelUnstructuredGrid

Reads a partitioned VTK XML unstructured grid: the .pvtu summary file plus the per-piece .vtu files it lists, typically written by an MPI run. The result is an unstructured grid with the point and cell arrays of all pieces. Use it to reopen distributed volume output, including Schemaxis's native parallel geometry (examples/schemaxis/foam-native-parallel.json); it is in Schemaxis's MPI-qualified operation list. Use readUnstructuredGrid for a single .vtu file.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- The .pvtu summary refers to its piece files by relative path; move them together.
- Ghost cells or duplicated interface points between pieces can affect counts and integrals; check vtkGhostType or clean the grid when exact counts matter.

Native constructor: `XMLPartitionedUnstructuredGridReader`. Identity: `sources/XMLPUnstructuredGridReader`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

No connected inputs (source/resource).


### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `files` | The list of files to be read by the reader. Each file is expected to be in the partitioned VTK XML unstructured grid data format. The standard extension is .pvtu. If more than one file is specified, the reader will switch to file series mode in which it will pretend that it can support time and provide one file per time step. Fixed at construction; cannot vary per visit. | `{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string","minLength":1},"minItems":1,"maxItems":1}` | `required` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |

Execution contract:

```json
{
  "mode": "serial",
  "performance": "unknown"
}
```

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "readParallelUnstructuredGrid",
  "options": {
    "files": [
      "REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"
    ]
  }
}
```
